BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI
 In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy   )
 Missouri Metro’s Request for Authority to          )   Case No. ER-2026-0143
 Implement a General Rate Increase for Electric     )
 Service
                 ORDER SHORTENING TIME TO OBJECT TO
                    STIPULATION AND AGREEMENTS

Issue Date: October 5, 2026                             Effective Date: October 5, 2026

       On October 2, 2026, Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro (Evergy

Metro) and the Commission’s Staff filed a Partial Stipulation and Agreement, a Non-

Unanimous Stipulation and Agreement Regarding Pensions and Other Post-Employment

Benefits, and a Partial Stipulation and Agreement - Non-C&I Rate Design.

       On October 5, 2026, Evergy Metro and Google LLC filed an LLPS Partial

Stipulation and Agreement. Also on October 5, 2026, Evergy Metro and Midwest Energy

Consumers Group filed a Non-Unanimous Partial Settlement - Rate Design. All five

stipulation and agreements are non-unanimous.

       Commission Rule 20 CSR 4240-2.115(2) provides that parties have seven days to

object to a non-unanimous stipulation and agreement. The seven days for parties to

respond to the stipulations and agreements extends well into the evidentiary hearing and

places objections due on October 9 and 12, 2026. Accordingly, the time for objections to

the stipulation and agreements will be shortened.

       THE COMMISSION ORDERS THAT:

       1.     Any objections to the five non-unanimous stipulations and agreements must

be filed no later than midnight on October 7, 2026.
       2.     This order is effective when issued.


                                        BY THE COMMISSION



                                        Nancy Dippell
                                        Secretary




John T. Clark, Senior Regulatory Law Judge,
